gpus.name: NVIDIA T4
gpus.notes: Cheapest GPU on Modal. No BF16 tensor cores, no async copy. FP16/INT8 tensor cores only. Up to 8 per container. ~50.8h on the $30/mo Starter credit.

gpus.name: NVIDIA L4
gpus.notes: Ada. Has FP8 tensor cores (E4M3/E5M2) but no TMA and no wgmma. Up to 8 per container. ~37.5h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA A10
gpus.notes: Canonical string is 'A10'. The legacy alias 'A10G' still appears in Modal's own current docs examples (guide/cuda) and still resolves. Max 4 GPUs per container (all other types allow 8). ~27.3h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA L40S
gpus.notes: Modal's explicitly recommended default for inference: 'we recommend starting off with the L40S, which offers an excellent trade-off of cost and performance and 48 GB of GPU RAM'. FP8, no TMA/wgmma. ~15.4h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA A100, 40 GB
gpus.notes: Plain gpu="A100" requests this tier but Modal 'may automatically upgrade a gpu="A100" request to run on an 80 GB A100' at no extra cost. Use 'A100-40GB' to pin 40GB. First arch with async copy (cp.async) and BF16. ~14.3h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA A100, 80 GB
gpus.notes: Same sm_80 target as the 40GB part; only HBM capacity/bandwidth differ. ~12h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell Server Edition)
gpus.notes: TRAP FOR FP4 CURRICULUM: this is Blackwell but it is the GB202 workstation die, compute capability 12.0, NOT the sm_100 datacenter Blackwell. It has 5th-gen tensor cores with FP4, but it does NOT have tcgen05 / the sm_100a datacenter tensor-core instructions. sm_100-targeted PTX/kernels will NOT run here. VRAM/arch/sm are from NVIDIA, not documented by Modal. ~9.9h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA H100 SXM5
gpus.notes: Modal states 'All H100 and H200 GPUs on the Modal platform are of the SXM variant'. Modal 'may automatically upgrade a gpu="H100" request to run on an H200' at no extra cost; pass gpu="H100!" to forbid that (matters for benchmarking). Modal's own docs use TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0 9.0a" for H100. TMA + wgmma + FP8. ~7.6h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 (no H200 upgrade)
gpus.notes: Same hardware and price as 'H100'; the trailing '!' opts out of the silent H200 upgrade. Use this for any benchmarking lesson where the learner must know exactly which chip they are on.

gpus.name: NVIDIA H200 SXM
gpus.notes: 141 GB HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s, explicitly stated in Modal's GPU guide. Same sm_90a target as H100 - a kernel compiled for one runs on the other. ~6.6h on $30.

gpus.name: NVIDIA B200
gpus.notes: AVAILABLE AND SELF-SERVE. This is the part your FP4/sm_100 curriculum needs: 5th-gen tensor cores, tcgen05, native FP4 (NVFP4/MXFP4). Requires CUDA 12.8+ toolkit in your image. ~4.8h on $30 - the FP4 lesson must be short.

gpus.name: NVIDIA B200 or B300 (opt-in upgrade pool)
gpus.notes: Modal: 'Use gpu="B200+" to allow Modal to run requests on either B200 or B300 GPUs. B200+ is billed as B200, regardless of which GPU is used.' Cheaper capacity access, but the learner no longer knows which SM they got - BAD for a teaching runner where the arch is the lesson. Requires CUDA 13.1+ because it may land on B300.

gpus.name: NVIDIA B300 (Blackwell Ultra)
gpus.notes: Most expensive. Modal: 'B300 requires CUDA version 13.1+. Make sure your container Image and libraries are compatible with CUDA 13 before requesting a B300.' sm_103a is from NVIDIA, not documented by Modal - VERIFY on-device with torch.cuda.get_device_capability(). ~4.2h on $30.
